engagement_title: Apex Rally Club collectible pack: recover six club faces off garage lit reference sheets, separate them for a twelve dollar pin and a ninety five dollar struck coin, and run the backing cards and the capsule collateral
vertical: Amateur motorsport club merchandise, hard enamel pins and struck challenge coins, a volunteer run rally club in Vermont selling at event tents and to a members list across New England and eastern Canada
real_brief_anchor: Anchored to the Upwork logo and challenge coin vectorization brief carried in the ledger (cand_38, db_i 95): the client already HAS hand mocked concept art and needs it turned into polished true vector artwork for a primary crest plus several symbolic coin face designs, coin ready and readable at small sizes, with versions reproducing in flat black, reversed white, and struck gold and silver metal, deliverable as clean scalable vector plus product ready exports for a mint handoff. The posting names no client, so the line is laundered to a coined fictional Western amateur motorsport club, the Apex Rally Club of Vermont. The ledger concedes that inventing new coin faces is not connector work; CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) makes the honest fuller commission real, because an ink level trace off photographed printed reference genuinely recovers existing faces, masked hue moves off one geometry genuinely produce colourways, a flat press PDF genuinely becomes a live record per page merge template with per row artwork binding, and HTML authoring genuinely produces a native editable document at true print canvases. Absorbs AO-38.
client_one_liner: We have reference sheets of our club crest and five event badges shot on a workbench under whatever light was in the garage, and a mint waiting on artwork for a twelve dollar pin and a ninety five dollar coin.
client_brief:
Apex Rally Club, collectible pack for the season finale

We are a volunteer run rally club in Vermont. Two hundred and forty members, six events a year, and a merch table that pays for the timing gear. This autumn we are doing our first proper collectible run with a mint: hard enamel pins and struck challenge coins.

The art already exists, more or less. The club crest goes back to 1987 and the five event badges were drawn over the years by members: the hillclimb, the night stage, the ice trial, the gravel loop and the finale. What we do not have is any of it as artwork a mint will accept. What we have is six reference sheets. They were printed at different times on different paper and photographed on a workbench under whatever light was in the garage that evening. Somebody also sent a photo of the crest as it is embroidered on the club jackets, in case it helps.

We need all six turned into artwork the mint can strike. They have told us the pins and the coins are not the same job. The pins are twelve dollars at the tent and they get simplified. The numbered coins are ninety five dollars, struck in a heavier metal, and members will hold one up to the light looking for the fine work. Same six designs, treated differently for each.

The crest also needs two or three colourways so the committee can pick one for the flagship coin. We want to see them next to each other on the metal rather than described in an email.

Then the merch table things. A backing card for each pin carrying its own code, edition size and price, print ready, and a card that sits in the coin capsule. Our printer has last year's backing card as a PDF and the six designs are in a spreadsheet.

And a sheet the mint can work from with the sizes, the metal and plating note, and the colours per design.

Tell us what will not strike and why.
price_band_and_audience: A two tier collectible line: twelve dollar impulse pins across a tent table and ninety five dollar numbered coins bought by members aged roughly twenty to forty five who already own the previous years. The band is load bearing and it splits the artwork in two. A struck coin at ninety five dollars has to carry fine raised line work and tight registration a member inspects in the hand, while a twelve dollar hard enamel pin has wells a mint must be able to fill, so detail below a certain weight has to be deliberately taken out rather than left in and hoped for. Treat the whole set at pin level and the coin reads as a giveaway and the numbered edition collapses; treat the pin at coin level and the mint cannot strike it, the enamel bleeds its wells and the tent table sells a defect. The register overall is club rather than corporate: confident and worn in rather than slick, never novelty and never distressed for effect, because the ninety five dollar buyer is buying continuity with 1987. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,400 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: apex_reference_sheets/ (6 frames, 4000 x 3000)
assets_supplied.kind: Photographs of the six printed reference sheets on a workbench: the club crest and five event badges, printed at different times on different stock.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The crest and the five event badges. Printed at different times, shot on the bench."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Line weight in a trace is set by how heavily the ink reads in the raster the trace receives rather than by how the badge was drawn, so six sheets photographed at six different exposures trace into six outlines whose strokes do not match, each looking correct alone. One sheet is on kraft toned stock where the ochre ink runs close in value to the paper along the badge's outer arc, so the isolation there succeeds and quietly bites that arc.

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is thread rather than ink, so the mark has no edge to isolate: a selection returns the jacket panel or a ragged patch shaped blob, and a trace returns a scalloped outline that reads as a manufacturing defect rather than the crest. It also carries a stitched year band the printed crest sheet does not have.

acceptance_bar: The six faces are ONE system. Laid out together at the sizes they are struck, stroke weight, corner treatment and detail level read as matched. A set that only matches when each is viewed alone fails.

The pin face and the coin face of a design are genuinely different reductions of it, defensible against a twelve dollar pin and a ninety five dollar coin. The same file at two sizes is one treatment, not two.
Every face is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent ground, a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle underneath.
The raised metal version of every face is line only and closed, with no filled interior where the struck metal should show through.
The colour version of every face uses no more colours than the mint's note allows, and the spec sheet's colour list is read off the artwork rather than off the intention.
Each of the six SKUs carries its own face on its own backing card. No card carries another SKU's art, and no proof is trusted because of where it fell in a list.
The backing card run is one print ready file with one card per SKU, plus a proof of each at true card resolution.
Every code, edition size and price is present in full at trim and reads back to the spreadsheet, including the rows the spreadsheet writes inconsistently.
The crest colourways are shown beside each other on one page at the size the coin is struck and on the metal it is struck in, not as swatches on white.
The spec sheet, capsule insert and colourway page arrive as ONE editable document with real text we can retype and the faces as live vector, delivered with the source it was built from.
The note says plainly which of the six will not strike as drawn, what was changed and why, and anything our printer has to be told about their own card file.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, upload every asset against its role and its SKU, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: Six cards each carrying a different picture is a record per page run; the spec sheet, insert and colourway page need an authored canvas. Identity has to be tracked from the first minute or it is guessed at later.
trajectory.produces: A surface plan, the confirmed tier, and a manifest keyed by design and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all six sheets and the jacket photograph and triage them for medium, ink to paper separation on each stock, exposure and design identity, then straighten what is off square.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes these are six pictures of six drawings. They are six printings on different stocks under different light, plus one that is thread rather than ink and therefore a different job entirely.
trajectory.produces: A per source triage note and levelled sheet masters where needed.

trajectory.action: Bring the six sheets to one target so the ink reads at one density, correcting each toward that destination with its own call and recording what was applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set rather than six good photographs, and one shared correction applied to six differently exposed frames is the wrong instrument. This is the last cheap moment to make the six comparable.
trajectory.produces: Six sheet masters at one ink density with a per sheet parameter log.

trajectory.action: Isolate the mark on each sheet by naming the ink's own visual properties rather than the sheet it is printed on, set the polarity the trace needs, and crop each to its own returned extent.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the sheet returns a paper shaped blob every later step processes as if it were the badge, and the kraft toned stock does not separate the way the white stocks do. Polarity is the difference between a positive face and a black box.
trajectory.produces: Six isolated plates at native scale.

trajectory.action: Flatten each isolated plate so the trace receives an edge rather than a print texture, then trace all six.
trajectory.judgement: The trace takes no options at all, so anything that will be true of the geometry has to be made true in the raster first. This is the only lever anywhere in the recovery.
trajectory.produces: Six traced faces plus a record of what was flattened per face.

trajectory.action: Do the vector hygiene on all six, injecting a real viewBox and removing the full canvas ground path, then lay the six out together at the sizes they are actually struck and judge them as a set.
trajectory.judgement: Six faces judged one at a time are not judged. The pack is a pack, and the only place a mismatch is visible is side by side at struck size.
trajectory.produces: Six hygienic faces and a set level judgement of how they sit together.

trajectory.action: Build the two reductions per design: the coin's line only raised metal plate carrying the fine work, and the pin's simplified hard enamel version with wells a mint can fill.
trajectory.judgement: This is the price band made physical. What comes out of the pin version is a craft decision about what the design can lose and still be itself, and it is what the mint will judge the pack on.
trajectory.produces: Twelve production faces, two per design, each off that design's one geometry.

trajectory.action: Fill the enamel version within the mint's colour ceiling, then produce two or three crest colourways as masked hue moves off the ONE crest geometry.
trajectory.judgement: Separate colourings drift and the mint receives three slightly different crests. The colour ceiling is a manufacturing constraint, so a fill that exceeds it is not a design choice, it is an unstrikeable file.
trajectory.produces: Six enamel faces within the ceiling plus crest colourways sharing one geometry.

trajectory.action: License a struck metal ground at full resolution with short generic queries filtered to photography, grade it to sit with the faces, then create the committee board and place the colourways, faces and ground within the per call cap.
trajectory.judgement: The colourways have to be approved on the material they will exist in. A partial board placement is reported as a success and vector is not placeable there, so what goes on the board is a deliberate choice.
trajectory.produces: A graded metal ground and a persistent committee board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's backing card PDF into a working layout, export its interchange form, and read what came back: the real frame inventory, whether any frame can carry a picture at all, and the real story text.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card shows a picture area and four lines of type. What the conversion produced is a different question, and it decides whether a per record face is even possible on this template.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory including graphic frames, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against the reconstructed story text, validate it, prepare the merge template, then export the rebuilt document again and confirm every placeholder is genuinely present.
trajectory.judgement: Both the validator and the template builder report success on a mapping whose positions are wrong, so reading the rebuilt document is the only trustworthy confirmation.
trajectory.produces: A verified merge template with its placeholders confirmed by inspection.

trajectory.action: Merge the six SKUs into one print ready file, binding each design's own face through the spreadsheet's artwork column, then render a proof per SKU at true card resolution and check identity by the code and the face printed on it.
trajectory.judgement: Position in a returned list is not identity, and the label on a per record raster is not evidence. Six cards going to a printer is where a swapped face is discovered on the tent table.
trajectory.produces: One six card print ready file plus six identified proofs at card resolution.

trajectory.action: Build the type system, one recommendation call per role plus the style inventories for the real numeric weights and one laundered kit, then author one self contained HTML carrying the spec sheet, capsule insert and colourway comparison at their own canvases, faces as inline SVG in explicitly sized wrappers and the metal ground embedded as image data.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged between a club with a 1987 history and a document a mint works from. On the canvas, a photograph left as a reference is not a photograph and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system recorded per role and one export ready HTML carrying all three canvases.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, verify through the two channels that exist, the rendition for the first canvas and the returned markup for the rest, then write the mint handover and the club note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition only shows the first artboard, so the insert and the comparison page can be checked no other way. The mint reads the handover before it cuts a die.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an audited export, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the six recovered faces are a set. Stroke weight in a traced outline is a function of how heavy the ink reads in the raster the trace received, not of how the badge was drawn, so six sheets printed at different times and photographed under different light trace into six outlines of visibly different line weight, each of which looks completely right while it is being looked at alone. The trace reports nothing: no weight, no threshold, no simplification, and an identical response for a heavy face and a spindly one. The mismatch exists only in the comparison, at struck size.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the mismatch is a property of the relationship between six finished traces and cannot exist until all six exist. Doing it right first time presumes knowing, per sheet, how much ink density to add or remove before a trace that has no controls, which nothing reports. Nothing states it either: the client describes the photographs, not what a trace does with them. It is not a propagation re run, because the fix reaches back to per sheet preparation for specific faces only.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify which faces sit heavy and which thin against the set, go back to the ink density preparation for just those sheets, re trace, redo the hygiene, and lay the six out together again at struck size.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A mint receives six faces that are supposed to be one collection and cuts six dies at three different line weights, which on a numbered ninety five dollar coin sold on continuity with 1987 is exactly the defect the buyer holds it to the light to look for.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each backing card is actually carrying its own design. Two things are knowable only by running the merge: whether the printer's flat card converted into a layout that can carry a different picture per record at all, which depends on how the original file was built rather than on what the printed card shows, and whether the per record proofs are in the order they claim. The proofs render, they carry a label naming their row, and that label can be wrong while every file reports success, so a run named by position ships the ice trial's face on the gravel loop's card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because both facts exist only after a conversion and a merge that have already happened, and no parameter controls either. Nothing states it, since the client says the shape is right and the design changes. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different delivery route chosen for identity, plus a verification pass that reads each proof's own content against its row.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Establish identity by what is printed on each proof, re derive the per SKU files through a route whose ordering is trustworthy, reconcile the two rows pointing at one artwork file, and re check all six.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six hundred pins reach a tent table on backing cards carrying the wrong design's face and the wrong edition size, which is a reprint of the whole run and a refund line at the event the pack was made for.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the colourway decision rests on. The committee has to judge the crest colourways on struck metal, so the natural construction is the face carried over the metal ground with a sheen and an edge treatment that read as struck rather than printed. Those constructions do not survive intact: blending against the ground and layered edge treatment are normalised away or truncated, silently, at full success, so the face can arrive as a flat opaque shape on a photograph of metal. The returned markup is the only channel that reports it, and the rendition shows the first canvas only.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports. Nothing states it: the client asks to see the colourways on the metal, which is art direction rather than a warning. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different upstream asset or a treatment rebuilt from the constructions that do survive.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the colourway page around a construction that survives the import, re author, re run the readiness check, export again, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A committee votes on a flagship coin colourway from a page where the crest is a flat shape on a picture of metal, picks the option that looks best flat, and the mint strikes the one that reads worst in the hand.

deliverables.name: Apex face system, six designs in two reductions plus crest colourways
deliverables.spec: Six club faces recovered from photographed printed reference as placeable scalable geometry with transparent grounds, a real viewBox present and no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along. Each in two genuine reductions, a line only closed raised metal plate for the struck coin and a simplified hard enamel version whose wells a mint can fill, plus two or three crest colourways derived as masked moves off one crest geometry. Stroke weight, corner treatment and detail level matched across the set at struck size.

deliverables.name: Pin backing card run
deliverables.spec: One print ready file carrying the six SKUs at one card per page, each bound to its own design's face and carrying its own code, edition size and tent price in full at trim, plus a proof of each SKU at true card resolution whose identity is established by the code and the face printed on it. Accompanied by the reconciliation of the two rows that pointed at one artwork file and of the inconsistent price and edition cells.

deliverables.name: Mint spec sheet, capsule insert and colourway comparison as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying three canvases: the mint specification with sizes, metal and plating and the per design colour list, the coin capsule insert, and the crest colourway comparison at struck size on the metal ground. Faces as live vector, real retypable text in one licensed type system, the metal ground embedded rather than referenced, delivered with the self contained source.

deliverables.name: Reference sheet masters and metal ground
deliverables.spec: The six reference sheets straightened and brought to one ink density target so the set is comparable, with a per sheet parameter log, plus one licensed camera scale struck metal frame graded to sit with the faces. No output exceeding its source dimensions and every reported resize recorded.

deliverables.name: Mint handover, club note and committee board
deliverables.spec: A written handover a mint can cut dies from and the club can read: sizes, metal and plating per design, the colour list read off the delivered artwork, what was simplified out of each pin face and why, which of the six will not strike as drawn, whether the embroidered crest was admissible and what the two crest versions disagree about, the type system by role with family, foundry and actual weight, and what the printer must change. Paired with a persistent committee board.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are a record per page run with per record artwork and which need an authored fixed canvas, since only one surface does each.
Whether the embroidered crest is admissible evidence at all, and which crest version is the club's when the two disagree about a year band.
How the isolation is worded per sheet, since naming the sheet returns paper and naming the ink's own visual properties returns the badge, and kraft stock does not behave like white stock.
How much correction to spend making six garage lit sheets comparable before any is traced, given that the trace has no controls at all.
What comes out of each pin face and what stays in each coin face, the price band expressed as craft and what the mint will judge the pack on.
Whether the colourways come off one geometry or off separate colourings, identical on delivery day and drifted within a season.
Whether the printer's card can carry a per record picture at all, and what to deliver instead if it cannot.
How to reconcile two rows pointing at one artwork file before anything is bound, and how to normalise the inconsistent price and edition cells without editing the client's meaning.
What to put in front of the committee, given that the board cannot carry vector and a colourway approved on white is not approved on metal.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the sheets into a frontier image model and it returns six handsome motorsport badges. IDENTITY: these are this club's actual crest from 1987 and five badges drawn by named members, worn on jackets and already owned by two hundred and forty people, so a regenerated badge is a different club's badge and the ninety five dollar coin is sold precisely on continuity with what already exists. SPEC: a mint needs closed line only geometry inside a stated diameter and a colour count ceiling, six cards at one SKU per page each bound to its own face with codes and edition sizes that reconcile to a spreadsheet, and proofs whose identity is provable. A generated picture satisfies none of that. EDITABILITY: the mint, the printer and next season's committee need real geometry and real editable documents, and the colour list has to be readable off the artwork rather than asserted.
